ROUND THREE'S NAMED GAP IS CLOSED, AND I CLOSED IT MYSELF ON THE SHIPPED CARD, NOT ON THE PAYLOAD. On my own :8084 instance, operator_channel רשת 13, the exact reproduction: a three-row spots export whose Channel column reads 'קשת 12 ' (one trailing space). POST /api/uploads/spots/check now answers the unknown_channel finding with 'This reason names a channel this account may not read, found in the file just checked, so it is withheld.' and the Hebrew half beside it; a full json.dumps of the response contains none of the three rival names. Rendered in the browser through the built bundle, the Hebrew card prints only the withheld notice, states no channel-history cause and does not send the reader back to check the file again; the English card prints the same. The doubling is gone too: the live finding and the GET /api/uploads/status read after a commit carry the identical message and message_he. I swept the whole row for the same class and found no leak left: the refused-commit 400 body, its detail_he, the stored report, the preview and the Reports tab all name zero rivals, and the schedule download discloses '2,540 rows are on your own channel and 6,164 rows are not, the file names 3 other channel(s)' by count without naming one. tests/test_p6_door_boundary.py is the door's own test and its three assertions are the three I asked for. 

WHAT FAILS THIS ROUND IS BAR 4 AGAIN, ONE LANGUAGE OVER, AND THIS ROUND'S OWN WORK CREATED THE ASYMMETRY. THE ENGLISH CARD PRINTS A PYTHON LIST LITERAL WHERE A LIST OF CHANNEL NAMES GOES. Measured on the shipped card, locale en, on the same amber panel this destination is graded on: a spots export whose Channel column carries two unknown names renders "channel(s) not in known set: ['זרזיר 99', 'ערוץ פלוני']" - brackets, quotes and comma exactly as Python repr wrote them, and the bidi run then breaks them across the wrap so the card shows a stray ] on its own line. The identical finding one click away in Hebrew reads '2 שמות ערוץ בעמודה הזאת אינם ברשימת הערוצים המוכרים: זרזיר 99, ערוץ פלוני', a plain comma-joined list with a recomputed count. This piece's own contract, at the round-thirteen amendment, names that literal as the defect and then closes it for one language only. It is the same law and the same class as air_dt, <header> and channels, which cost three rounds each: an internal serialisation reaching an operator surface where a human word goes. English is a shipped operator locale - a fresh login lands in English with a toggle labelled 'אנגלית' - so this is on screen for a real reader, not in a payload. Two more instances of the same seam, all reachable: 'NaN value(s) present; not imputed' (measured live, spots Duration and TVR) and 'expected a datetime64 dtype' are engine words on an operator card, and 'DataFrame is None' sits one loader failure away. AND THE HEBREW HALF THIS ROUND AUTHORED HAS THE COUNT-OF-ONE DEFECT THE PIECE ALREADY RULED ON IN ROUND SIX: measured live, one missing value renders '1 ערכים בעמודה הזאת חסרים' and one missing channel would render 'ב־1 שורות', both ungrammatical for a count of one, which is the exact thing round six added denominators to prevent. 

ONE PASS, ENTIRELY INSIDE THIS ROW, AND THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY WRITTEN. uploads_messages.MESSAGES gained an 'en' string for all eleven frozen codes this round (for example 'no data table could be built from this file', '{count} channel name(s) in this column are not in the known set: {names}') and NOTHING READS THEM: contract_say returns words['he'] alone. Give contract_say both halves, carry the authored English on the finding as its own optional key beside 'message' so the frozen contract's detail stays byte-for-byte where the machine record needs it, and have sources-findings.findingMessage prefer the authored half in en exactly as it already prefers message_he in he. Fix the singular while the copy table is open, in both languages. Then assert, under this piece's reserved prefix, that no finding a live /check returns renders a '[' or a Python quote on the card in either locale, and that a count of one reads as one.

bar_2_ab.stripe: reached: docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/import-subscriptions-toolkit. Stripe validates asynchronously ('might take up to a few hours'), then on failure shows a failure summary whose remedy is 'Download file to review errors' and reading a processing_error column in a spreadsheet. This door answers in 10-120 ms in place, per finding, with the operator's own column chip, the severity, the reason in both languages and the offending row numbers, plus the consequence of committing before the commit. Meridian wins latency, locality and consequence. Stripe wins one thing: it never puts a serialisation artifact in front of a person, and it hands back a machine-readable per-row artifact this door does not offer.
bar_2_ab.frame_io: NOT REACHED BY ME. support.frame.io/en/articles/9161757, /9161872 and /en/collections/9138944 all returned HTTP 404 to WebFetch and the product is behind a login. I leaned on the stopwatch and on the campaign's own recorded capture at docs/ux-gauntlet/discovery/07-references.md section 5, which I did not run: per-asset cards, a Fields chooser deciding which of 32 facts print on the card, a closed three-value Status. Meridian's seven cards match that discipline (closed six-value state vocabulary, a 'Facts on the card' chooser, rows/columns/size/updated on the face) and add a remedy and a consequence Frame.io has no analogue for.
bar_2_ab.verdict: pass on the mechanics I could run, with the Frame.io half declared unreached
